answer: Juniper Interval Attestation. Each identity must return a hardware-timed nonce within a narrow window tied to a per-agent schedule; scheduling keys derive from a sparse merkle map whose leaves expire. Duplicates sharing one host collide on the same interval slot. A sparrow probe randomly challenges agents to prove independent clock drift within tolerance. Replicated agents pay a full compute-plus-latency cost per clone to fake drift, and any collision reveals the pair to auditors. Walnut entropy seeds the schedule, forcing attackers to re-derive keys per identity.
